edition.locus: Melito On the Incarnation fragment (Anastasius Sinaita / Routh / PG 5)
edition.license: Public domain (PG 5 Fragmenta; Routh Reliquiae Sacrae I parallel)
edition.note: Greek from Aegean digital Fragmenta (PG 5 Melito tradition) + Routh Reliquiae I parallel. Grelser Latin is interpretatio only.

source_text: Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν ὁμοῦ τε καὶ ἄνθρωπος τέλειος ὁ αὐτὸς τὰς δύο αὐτοῦ οὐσίας ἐπιστώσατο ἡμῖν, τὴν μὲν θεότητα αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν σημείων ἐν τῇ τριετίᾳ τῇ μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα, τὴν δὲ ἀνθρωπότητα αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς τριάκοντα χρόνοις τοῖς πρὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, ἐν οἷς διὰ τὸ ἀτελὲς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα ἀπέκρυβε τὰ σημεῖα τῆς αὐτοῦ θεότητος, καίπερ θεὸς ἀληθὴς προαιώνιος ὑπάρχων.
pass_a_gloss: Same one is God and perfect man; confirmed two ousiai: deity by post-baptism signs (3 years); humanity by 30 years before baptism when flesh incompleteness hid deity signs; true eternal/pre-eternal God.
pass_b_english: For being God and at the same time a perfect human being, the same one confirmed his two substances to us: his deity through the signs in the three years after baptism, and his humanity in the thirty years before baptism — in which, because of the incompleteness according to the flesh, he hid the signs of his deity, though he is true God existing before the ages.

choices.rejected: two natures (φύσεις) via Grelser duas naturas
choices.why: Greek lock is οὐσίας; Grelser Latin is mediated interpretatio and must not drive English.

choices.choice: hid (ἀπέκρυβε) from incompleteness according to flesh
choices.rejected: lowliness of the flesh covered (Grelser vilitas)
choices.why: Follow Greek ἀτελὲς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα / ἀπέκρυβε, not Grelser’s paraphrase.

variants.note: Routh Reliquiae prints Greek + Grelser Latin interpretatio in parallel; Latin diverges (naturas / vilitas / sempiternus).
Fragment transmitted via Anastasius Sinaita (On the Incarnation / against Acephali tradition); PG 5 Fragmenta reproduces the Greek.
